summary: Follow-up postmortem for a transient eviction surge that caused 5–10s tail latency for embeddings routes. Root cause narrowed to aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction under bursty concat workloads plus an autoscaler interaction. Agreed next steps include a hotfix (raise eviction watermark, conservative autoscale cooldown), bench runs, and a scheduled canary rollout.
topics: Root cause hypothesis (cache eviction + autoscaler interaction)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start: 15:00 PDT (2026-09-10T22:00Z)
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Marcus Vela (Redwood); Sofia Morales, Liam O'Connor, Dr. Anya Patel, Ethan Brooks (Catalyst)

Summary (auto): quick postmortem, confirm hotfix and canary plan, list action owners

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): okay everyone thanks for joining, um we know this is a follow-up to the outage window last friday, appreciate you carving time
[00:14] Sofia (Catalyst VP Eng): yeah thanks, we still have customer tickets coming in today so wanted to make sure we closed the loop on the root cause and the rollout plan
[00:28] Marcus (Redwood CSM): quick agenda — timeline, root cause hypothesis, hotfix, bench plan, canary plus rollback, wilson? sorry i mean questions
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): i'll start with a quick recap of telemetry — we saw a sharp increase in embeddings route tail latency around 10:12 UTC, spike lasted approx 7 minutes with repeated ~5 to 10 second tails on 95/99
[01:05] Liam (Catalyst Platform): yah, and for context we were running a batch of nightly productization concat jobs that were creating many long prefixes, so a lot of KV lookups per request
[01:22] Priya: exact — the pattern was many small concurrent sessions which each touched long prefix chains, this exposed a behavior in our prefix caching where entries were evicted too eagerly under mem pressure
[01:37] Alex: quick dumb question — is this the K-V cache or the prefix cache? I heard both used in notes
[01:44] Priya: sorry, yeah i use them interchangeably — it's the prefix KV cache inside the serving runtime; sometimes transcription writes K-V cash, this is a long-standing handwriting of the logs
[01:56] Anya (SecOps): i want to call out the autoscaler interaction — our logs show a scale-down event during the spike window, which reduced headroom and made eviction pressure worse
[02:12] Priya: exactly, two factors: threshold configuration that was too aggressive (low watermark) and a scale decision that cut pods when a short burst cleared queue length metrics; by the time pods came back the rewarm of cache led to high remote hits and long tails
[02:30] Ethan (SRE): we saw a sympathetic effect on downstream rerankers as well, that amplified timeouts in our API layer, so compound failure mode
[02:45] Marcus: ok that's useful. can you run through the concrete hotfix you folks proposed?
[02:50] Priya: short version: raise eviction watermark by 30%, add a soft-lru hold window for recently accessed keys (reduce churn), and increase autoscaler cooldown to 180s for the embeddings route. We also add more conservative scheduler hints so that bursty concat jobs don't trigger immediate scale down
[03:12] Sofia: if we raise watermark, that means memory will be higher — any OOM risk?
[03:20] Priya: we ran mem projections — in our dev cluster the increase is about 12% headroom on the serving node; it's safe with current instance types but if you have tight memory we can instead enable a partial sticky cache option (trade higher latency for lower mem)
[03:38] Liam: what's the rollback plan if this hotfix makes memory bump too big in prod?
[03:44] Alex: good point — rollback is immediate config revert and forced cache purge, plus a short-term fallback to a smaller model variant routed by policy. We'll document the runbook in the canary notes
[03:58] Priya: also want to call out an alternative we discussed: dedicated reserved capacity for high-throughput jobs so those concat bursts don't fight with low-latency traffic. That is a longer sales/ops conversation though
[04:14] Sofia: we want the hotfix now, dedicated cap can be follow-up. Ok please share cost delta for that too
[04:20] Alex: noted — we'll include a ballpark of monthly cost delta for dedicated reserved capacity in the follow-up brief
[04:30] [05:00] Priya: next, validation plan — we propose two bench runs: stage full concurrency (1000 concurrent sessions, mimic production prefix lengths) and a synthetic burst test where we push 3x normal qps for 10 minutes. We measure 95/99, remote hit ratio, and eviction churn metrics
[05:24] Ethan: can you also export the prefix map so we can correlate hot keys? Last time we were blind there was a densification effect
[05:32] Priya: yeah we'll provide prefix map + sample keys redacted; note some names might be misparsed in transcription but we'll keep the artifact clean
[05:45] [07:05] Liam: timeline — when can you get the hotfix build?
[07:12] Priya: target is EOD monday our time, so that's 2026-09-12. We can push a build and smoke benchmark notes same day
[07:22] Sofia: ok good. can we get the bench results by Wednesday?
[07:26] Marcus: i'll help coordinate the bench window with your ops; recommended canary window is Thursday 02:00-04:00 UTC to minimize customer impact
[07:36] Anya: on compliance side — we need to ensure audit logging is intact during the canary. The change touches cache behavior but should not alter PII logging; still, we want a grepable log for the window
[07:50] Alex: understood, we'll include a logging verification checklist: SSO traces, request IDs, KMS call counts, that sort of thing
[07:58] [09:10] Priya: I also want to mention a follow-up medium-term fix — smarter eviction policy: frequency-aware retention for keys with high re-use, might require a small store for hot-key counters. That is a 2–3 sprint feature
[09:30] Sofia: can we get a proposal doc for that? We need to choose whether to invest vs buy reserved capacity
[09:36] Priya: yes i'll write a short proposal and include cost/benefit and risk summary
[09:44] [11:00] Ethan: heads up — we also saw some noisy GC events on the serving host in the past month; might be contributing, i've filed a separate ticket but want to flag it here
[11:12] Priya: thanks ethan, that helps. if GC coincides with scale decisions we get a compounding effect
[11:20] [13:05] Liam: question on observability — where will the eviction/churn metrics live? we want dashboards and alerts, not just logs
[13:12] Priya: we'll push a dashboard to your prometheus bundle and add alert thresholds for eviction_rate > 0.2 and remote_hit_ratio < 0.6 for >2 minutes. we'll also add a synthetic canary alert so the team sees regressions early
[13:30] Sofia: are these available in the console, or do we need to wire into our graphing?
[13:36] Marcus: Redwood Console will have a per-route dashboard; we'll also share a grafana dashboard you can import
[13:44] [16:00] Alex: let's talk comms — who owns customer messaging?
[16:06] Sofia: i'll take initial customer-facing note for impacted accounts; i'll need a short RCA paragraph and reassurance of the fix timeline
[16:15] Marcus: we'll draft an engineering summary and share with you for redline; also will include suggested escalation contact list and canary times
[16:28] [18:00] Anya: security question — the autoscaler change is config only? no code that touches KMS or credentials?
[18:08] Priya: config + runtime flags only, no new secrets. We'll keep KMS calls unchanged; Anya, we'll loop you in to validate the checklist
[18:20] [20:00] Sofia: are we comfortable that this won't impact other tenant workloads? we run multi-tenant instances on the cluster
[20:08] Priya: yes design is tenant-aware. the soft-hold window is applied at the route level so it's scoped to embeddings route for your account; we'll verify cross-tenant memory metrics in the bench results
[20:32] [24:00] Liam: can you show the rough command sequence for the canary and rollback?
[24:12] Priya: sure — 1) flip flag in config store to new eviction watermark, 2) deploy hotfix image to canary subset, 3) run synthetic smoke tests for 20m, 4) monitor 95/99 and eviction churn, 5a) if green -> expand 20% every 10 min, 5b) if regress -> revert config and image, purge cache and route to variant model. we'll produce a runbook doc with exact kubectl/console steps
[24:52] [28:00] Marcus: ok sounds good. risk callouts?
[28:05] Priya: residual risk is memory pressure leading to OOM on worst-case nodes — mitigated by phased canary and immediate rollback. Also slightly higher request tail if sticky keys rewarm slowly; bench should reveal magnitude
[28:28] Sofia: what about predictable costs? if we recommend dedicated reserved capacity, need procurement signoff
[28:36] Alex: i'll include a cost delta and a procurement note; Marcus can help with an SOW if needed
[28:48] [32:00] Ethan: i want to record that we need full request traces with request IDs preserved; that was a gap last incident
[32:08] Priya: yes we'll enable a trimmed trace window for the canary and give you a sanitized trace dump after the run
[32:24] [34:00] Sofia: anything else?
[34:04] Marcus: quick recap of next steps (we'll email): hotfix build by 9/12 (Priya), prefix map + bench artifacts (Priya), canary scheduling (Marcus & Liam), smoke tests by customer (Liam) and compliance verification (Anya).
[34:26] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with a Slack thread and a shared folder (link: https://redwood.app/briefs/ff-15842-hotfix) with artifacts
[34:40] Sofia: appreciate it, talk soon
[34:45] [36:00] Speaker 7: recording stopped

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K-V cash, R-back for RBAC, V-P-C written out). We kept the technical content intentionally terse in transcript; artifacts in the shared folder will contain the precise runbook and bench configs.
